Governor Kehoe Announces Seven Gubernatorial Appointments

November 6, 2026

Jefferson City

Today, Governor Kehoe announced seven gubernatorial appointments to various boards and commissions.
Chief Floyd Blake III
, of Pacific, was appointed to the 
Missouri Fire Safety Education Advisory Commission
.
Chief Blake currently serves as fire chief for the City of Frontenac. He has served on the Meramec Ambulance District Board of Directors, holds a certificate from the St. Louis County Fire Academy, and is a licensed paramedic in Missouri. Blake is a graduate of Pacific High School.
Timothy Flora
, of Ellisville, was reappointed to the 
Missouri State Board of Private Investigators, Private Fire Investigators and Professional Surety Bail Bond Agents
.
Mr. Flora is president and a certified, licensed polygraph examiner at Mid-West Protective Service, Inc. He has served as director of the Metro West Fire Protection District and chairman of the Central County Emergency 911 Dispatch Center. Flora holds a certificate in criminal justice from Northeast Missouri State University, a Bachelor of Science in Management from Tarkio College, and a Master of Arts in Legal Studies from Webster University.
Gregory Frencken
, of Chilhowee, was reappointed to the 
Missouri Military Preparedness and Enhancement Commission
.
Mr. Frencken is the owner of Frencken Insurance and Financial Services, Inc. He is a civic leader for the Department of the Air Force, serving as a member of the Whiteman Air Force Base Community Council and president of the Whiteman Area Leadership Council. Frencken holds a Bachelor of Science in Health Services Management from the University of Missouri.
Charles Giessing
, of Farmington, was reappointed to the 
Missouri State Board of Private Investigators, Private Fire Investigators and Professional Surety Bail Bond Agents
.
Mr. Giessing is the owner and consultant of Pro-G Fire Consulting and has more than 47 years of experience in the public and private sectors. He is a member of the International Association of Arson Investigators, the Professional Fire and Fraud Investigators Association, and the National Association of Fire and Explosion Investigators. Giessing is a graduate of the Missouri State Highway Patrol Law Enforcement Academy and holds an Associate Degree in Criminal Justice from Mineral Area College.
Jason Olliges
, of St. Louis, was appointed to the 
Missouri Fire Safety Education Advisory Commission
.
Mr. Olliges works for Sprinkler Fitters Local 268. He is a member of the NFPA Technical Committee and the Advisory Committee for the Lindbergh School District. Olliges holds sprinkler fitter licenses in the City of St. Louis and St. Louis County and serves as a principal member of the NFPA Private Water Supply Technical Committee. He holds a Bachelor of Administration in Business Management and Information Systems from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville.
Roy Pace
, of Rogersville, was appointed to the 
Board of Nursing Home Administrators
.
Mr. Pace is an administrator at Colonial Springs Healthcare Center. He is a licensed nursing home administrator and registered nurse. He is a member of the Missouri Health Care Association Board of Directors and serves with the Dallas County Technical Institute and Bolivar Technical Institute advisory boards. Pace holds a Licensed Practical Nurse credential from the South-Central Career Center and a Registered Nurse credential from Missouri State University-West Plains.
Scott Ream
, of West Plains, was reappointed to the 
State Board of Optometry
.
Mr. Ream has owned and served as the primary optometrist at Scott Ream Optometry for nearly 40 years. He serves as president of the Missouri Optometric Foundation and as past president of the Missouri Optometric Association. He earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Missouri-Kansas City and his Doctor of Optometry from the University of Missouri-St. Louis College of Optometry.
